title: Rational opposition involution for a prescribed simple-root pinning
statement: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional semisimple $\mathbf Q$-Lie algebra [def-wf-lie-algebra], [def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak h\subseteq\mathfrak g$ be a maximal abelian subalgebra acting diagonally over $\mathbf Q$, with root decomposition $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in R}\mathfrak g_\alpha$, where $R\subset\mathfrak h^\vee\setminus\{0\}$ is its reduced crystallographic root system and $\mathfrak g_\alpha=\{z:[h,z]=\alpha(h)z\text{ for every }h\in\mathfrak h\}$ is one-dimensional. For $\alpha\in R$, let $h_\alpha\in[\mathfrak g_\alpha,\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}]\subseteq\mathfrak h$ be the coroot with $\alpha(h_\alpha)=2$. Fix a base $\Delta\subseteq R$, meaning a basis of $\mathfrak h^\vee$ such that every root has integral coordinates of one sign, and nonzero $x_\delta\in\mathfrak g_\delta$ for $\delta\in\Delta$. There is a $\mathbf Q$-linear Lie automorphism $\theta:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak g$ with $\theta^2=1$, $\theta(h)=-h$ for $h\in\mathfrak h$, and $\theta(\mathfrak g_\alpha)=\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$ for every root, such that $[x_\delta,-\theta(x_\delta)]=h_\delta$ for every $\delta\in\Delta$. The assertion includes $\Delta=\varnothing$.

source.place: Section 23h, printed p.508, opposition involution following the normalized simple-root triples; rational descent of this involution is an agent-stated supporting assertion, using the generator relations on pp.503--504, not a quotation of a rational-field theorem.

proof.text: Enumerate $\Delta=\{\alpha_i:i\in I\}$ and put $e_i=x_{\alpha_i}$. The split root-decomposition theorem gives rational $f_i\in\mathfrak g_{-\alpha_i}$ with $[e_i,f_i]=h_i:=h_{\alpha_i}$ and gives the spanning, integral and reflection-compatible root/coroot pairing for evaluation $\mathfrak h^\vee\times\mathfrak h\to\mathbf Q$. Apply the rational root-base theorem to this pairing and the given base: the $h_i$ form a basis of $\mathfrak h$. These hypotheses hold because the given $\mathfrak g$ is finite-dimensional semisimple and $\mathfrak h$ is maximal abelian and acts diagonally over $\mathbf Q$. If $I=\varnothing$, the given base forces $\mathfrak h^\vee=0$, hence $\mathfrak h=0$, $R=\varnothing$ and $\mathfrak g=0$ by the given decomposition; take its identity automorphism. Below assume $I\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.503--504 and p.508; rational generator-relations argument, with automorphism signs as in this item.

proof.text: Put $a_{ij}=\alpha_j(h_i)$. The pinned Serre-presentation lemma applies to the same split rational algebra, base and normalized pairs $e_i,f_i$. It supplies $\phi:\mathfrak s(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathfrak g$ sending $H_i,E_i,F_i$ to $h_i,e_i,f_i$, respectively. In particular every generator relation displayed in that lemma holds in $\mathfrak s(A)$, and $\mathfrak s(A)$ is the stated quotient of a free rational Lie algebra.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.503--504 and p.508; rational generator-relations argument, with automorphism signs as in this item.

proof.text:
On the free algebra set $T(H_i)=-H_i$, $T(E_i)=-F_i$, $T(F_i)=-E_i$ and extend by its defining universal property. Write $r^{EF}_{ij}=[E_i,F_j]-\delta_{ij}H_i$, $r^{HE}_{ij}=[H_i,E_j]-a_{ij}E_j$ and $r^{HF}_{ij}=[H_i,F_j]+a_{ij}F_j$. Bilinearity and skew-symmetry give $T([H_i,H_j])=[H_i,H_j]$, $T(r^{EF}_{ij})=-r^{EF}_{ji}$, $T(r^{HE}_{ij})=r^{HF}_{ij}$ and $T(r^{HF}_{ij})=r^{HE}_{ij}$. For $n=1-a_{ij}$, induction on the nested bracket gives
$$T((\operatorname{ad}E_i)^nE_j)=(-1)^{n+1}(\operatorname{ad}F_i)^nF_j,$$
and the same formula with $E,F$ exchanged. Thus $T$ sends each generating relator into the relator ideal $J$. The inverse image $T^{-1}(J)$ is an ideal containing those relators, so it contains $J$; hence $T$ descends to a rational Lie endomorphism $\tau$ of the quotient. Its square fixes every generator and therefore every rational linear combination of bracket words, so $\tau^2=1$.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.503--504 and p.508; rational generator-relations argument, with automorphism signs as in this item.

proof.text: Define $\theta=\phi\tau\phi^{-1}$. Then $\theta$ is a rational Lie automorphism, $\theta^2=1$, $\theta(e_i)=-f_i$ and $\theta(h_i)=-h_i$. Since the $h_i$ are a basis, $\theta(h)=-h$ on all of $\mathfrak h$. For $z\in\mathfrak g_\alpha$, applying $\theta$ to $[h,z]=\alpha(h)z$ gives $[-h,\theta z]=\alpha(h)\theta z$, or $[h,\theta z]=-\alpha(h)\theta z$. Hence $\theta(\mathfrak g_\alpha)\subseteq\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$, and applying the same calculation to $-\alpha$ and using $\theta^2=1$ gives equality. Finally $[x_{\alpha_i},-\theta(x_{\alpha_i})]=[e_i,f_i]=h_i$, as required.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.503--504 and p.508; rational generator-relations argument, with automorphism signs as in this item.

lean.statement: theorem exists_rational_opposition_involution (L : Type u) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℚ L] [FiniteDimensional ℚ L] [HasTrivialRadical ℚ L] (H : LieSubalgebra ℚ L) [IsLieAbelian H] (hmax : ∀ A : LieSubalgebra ℚ L, H ≤ A → IsLieAbelian A → A = H) (hsplit : ∀ h : H, (⨆ a : ℚ, (ad ℚ L (h : L)).eigenspace a) = ⊤) (I : Type v) [Finite I] (P : RootPairing I ℚ (Module.Dual ℚ H) H) [P.IsRootSystem] [P.IsCrystallographic] [P.IsReduced] (heval : ∀ (α : Module.Dual ℚ H) (h : H), P.toLinearMap α h = α h) (hdecomp : DirectSum.IsInternal (Sum.elim (fun _ : Unit ↦ H.toSubmodule) (fun i : I ↦ (LieModule.weightSpace L (P.root i)).toSubmodule))) (hdim : ∀ i : I, Module.finrank ℚ (LieModule.weightSpace L (P.root i)) = 1) (hcoroot : ∀ i : I, (P.coroot i : L) ∈ Submodule.span ℚ {z : L | ∃ a ∈ LieModule.weightSpace L (P.root i), ∃ b ∈ LieModule.weightSpace L (-P.root i), ⁅a, b⁆ = z}) (Δ : Set I) (b : Module.Basis Δ ℚ (Module.Dual ℚ H)) (hb : ∀ i : Δ, b i = P.root i) (hsign : ∀ i : I, P.root i ∈ AddSubmonoid.closure (P.root '' Δ) ∨ -P.root i ∈ AddSubmonoid.closure (P.root '' Δ)) (x : Δ → L) (hx : ∀ i : Δ, x i ∈ LieModule.weightSpace L (P.root i)) (hxne : ∀ i : Δ, x i ≠ 0) : ∃ θ : L ≃ₗ⁅ℚ⁆ L, Function.Involutive θ ∧ (∀ h : H, θ (h : L) = -(h : L)) ∧ (∀ i : I, Submodule.map θ.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap (LieModule.weightSpace L (P.root i)).toSubmodule = (LieModule.weightSpace L (-P.root i)).toSubmodule) ∧ (∀ i : Δ, ⁅x i, -θ (x i)⁆ = (P.coroot i : L))
